neutral_facts.value: The accused and the victim were strangers who engaged in a verbal altercation that escalated into a physical fight. The accused used dangerous weapons, including a sickle and sword, to assault the victim. The victim sustained severe injuries, including bleeding on his head, left paw, wrist, right hand, and right shoulder, and ultimately succumbed to his injuries. The victim was taken to a hospital where he was declared dead. The prosecution presented eyewitness accounts, medical evidence, and recovery of weapons. The trial court convicted the accused of murder under Section 302 of the IPC, and the High Court upheld the conviction. The accused claimed the case fell under Exception 4 to Section 300, but the Supreme Court rejected this, emphasizing the use of dangerous weapons and the victim's helplessness.

investigation_status.value: First information report lodged on 2.04.2002. The dead body of the deceased was sent for post mortem. The clothes of the deceased stained with blood were collected and sent to the forensic science laboratory for chemical analysis. The scene of offence panchnama was drawn. The clothes of all the accused were collected and sent to the FSL. The discovery panchnamas were drawn in presence of the panch witnesses. The statements of various other witnesses were recorded by the police. Chargesheet filed for the offence punishable under Section 302 read with Section 34 of the IPC.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that a verbal altercation between the parties resulted in a fight where the first informant was assaulted on the head and the deceased suffered severe assault leading to his death. The appellants were convicted under Section 302 r/w 34 and sentenced to life imprisonment. The High Court upheld the order, and the oral evidence of the three eyewitnesses was found to be consistent and reliable.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the initial burden to prove the case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt rests on the prosecution. It also emphasized that for a case to fall under Exception 4 to Section 300, all the ingredients mentioned in the exception must be found.

quotes.text: The initial burden to establish the case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt rests on the prosecution. It is also an elementary principle of law that the prosecution has to prove its case on its own legs and cannot derive advantage or benefit from the weakness of the defence.
